chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-Kahili, who said:
I asked him about Tayammum. He said, 'So he struck with his hand upon the rug, and wiped his face with it. Then he wiped his two hands, one of them upon the back of the other.'

key_terms.الْبِسَاط: The rug (used here as a representative surface for dust)

ai.seo_question: How is the ritual of Tayammum performed according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the practical flexibility of Tayammum, demonstrating that the 'earth' (turab) can be represented by any clean surface like a rug, rather than requiring direct contact with bare soil. It establishes the specific sequence of wiping the face followed by the hands, a procedure widely accepted in Shia fiqh as the standard method derived from the Imams. This hadith serves as a primary evidence for the simplicity and accessibility of dry ablution when water is unavailable or its use is harmful.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Safwan, from Al Kahily who said,
‘I asked himasws about the Tayammum. So heasws struck with hisasws hand upon the rug, and heasws wiped hisasws face with it. Then heasws wiped his wrists, one of them upon the back of the other’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from al-Kahiliy who has said the following: “
I once asked him (the Imam) about Tayammum. He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, thumped his hand on the furnishing, then wiped with it his face and then the backs of his both hands one with the other.”
